message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What you need | How it works | |---------|---------------|--------------| | **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (Red, Yellow, Green, Blue). Each color has numbers 0‑9 (two of each 1‑9, one 0) and two of each action card: Skip, Reverse, Draw Two. Plus 4 Wild cards and 4 Wild Draw Four cards. | Shuffle the deck and deal 7 cards to each player. Place the remaining cards face‑down to form the draw pile. Turn the top card over to start the discard pile. | | **Goal** | Be the first player to score **500 points** (or a pre‑agreed total). Points are tallied after each round. | | **Gameplay** | 1. Play proceeds clockwise (unless a Reverse changes direction). 2. On your turn, you may play **one** card that matches the discard pile’s **color**, **number**, or **action**. 3. If you can’t play, you must draw one card from the draw pile. If that card can be played, you may play it immediately; otherwise, your turn ends. | | **Action Cards** | • **Skip** – next player loses a turn.
• **Reverse** – changes play direction.
• **Draw Two** – next player draws two cards and loses a turn.
• **Wild** – you choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – you choose the new color; next player draws four cards and loses a turn. (Can only be played if you have no other playable card; otherwise, the opponent can challenge.) | | **Winning a Round** | When a player discards their last card, they shout “UNO!” if they have one card left. If they forget, the next player draws two penalty cards. The round ends when someone has no cards left. | | **Scoring** | • Number cards: face value.
• Skip, Reverse, Draw Two: 20 points each.
• Wild, Wild Draw Four: 50 points each.
Points are added to the winner’s score from the cards remaining in opponents’ hands. | | **Starting a New Round** | Shuffle the remaining cards, deal 7 again, and start with the next player clockwise. The first player to reach the target score wins the game. | --- ### Quick Tips 1. **Keep track of the color** – if you’re low on cards, try to play a Wild or Wild Draw Four to change the color to something you have more of. 2. **Use Draw Two/Draw Four strategically** – stack them on opponents if they’re about to win. 3. **Watch for “UNO”** – if you’re the second‑to‑last card, shout it loudly to avoid penalties. 4. **Challenge rule** – if you suspect a Wild Draw Four was played illegally, you can challenge. If you’re right, the offending player draws 4 cards; if wrong, you draw 6. Enjoy the fast‑paced, colorful fun of Uno!
